videos.title: One Word Can Change What You Remember Seeing
videos.topic: The misinformation effect: a single word in a question can change what people remember seeing, as shown in the classic car-crash memory experiment.
videos.genre: a surprising quirk of how memory works

videos.title: The Hidden Bias That Quietly Steers Your Guesses
videos.topic: Anchoring bias: the first number we hear pulls our later estimates toward it, shown in Tversky and Kahneman's rigged wheel experiment.
videos.genre: a hidden bias that shapes everyday decisions

videos.title: Why You Sing Quieter in a Group (Social Loafing)
videos.topic: Social loafing: people tend to put in less effort when their work is pooled in a group (the Ringelmann rope-pulling effect)
videos.genre: why people behave strangely in groups

videos.title: The Simple If-Then Trick That Beats Procrastination
videos.topic: Implementation intentions: making a specific if-then plan helps people follow through on goals more than a vague intention alone (Peter Gollwitzer's research).
videos.genre: the psychology of habits and procrastination
